    sigma_gps_time: f64,

    imu_accel_noise_density: f64,
    /// IMU gyroscope noise density (rad/s/√Hz) — consumer MEMS
    imu_gyro_noise_density: f64,
    /// IMU sample rate (Hz)
    imu_sample_rate: f64,
    /// Number of Monte Carlo trials
    n_trials: usize,
}

/// Result of one Monte Carlo trial.
struct TrialResult {
    /// True γ−1 for this trial
    true_gamma_minus_1: f64,
    /// Measured γ−1 from GPS speed (assumes SR formula)
    measured_gamma_minus_1: f64,
    /// Uncertainty on measured γ−1 from GPS speed uncertainty
    sigma_gamma_minus_1: f64,
    /// Measured transit time from GPS (s)
    gps_transit_time: f64,
    /// Uncertainty on GPS transit time (s)
    sigma_transit_time: f64,
    /// Transit-time-based bound on |γ−1|
    bound_from_timing: f64,
}

/// Run the full Monte Carlo simulation.
fn run_protocol(cfg: &ProtocolConfig) -> (Vec<TrialResult>, f64, f64) {
    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();
    let normal = Normal::new(0.0, 1.0).unwrap();

    let mut trials: Vec<TrialResult> = Vec::with_capacity(cfg.n_trials);

    for _ in 0..cfg.n_trials {
        // True speed: draw from a distribution around nominal speed
        // (car speed varies slightly between trials)
        let true_speed = cfg.nominal_speed + normal.sample(&mut rng) * 2.0; // σ_v = 2 m/s natural variation
        let true_beta = true_speed / C;
        let true_gamma = 1.0 / (1.0 - true_beta.powi(2)).sqrt();
        let true_gamma_minus_1 = true_gamma - 1.0;

        // True transit time in the tunnel frame
        let true_transit = cfg.tunnel_length / true_speed;

        // ── GPS measurements ──
        // GPS speed measurement (noisy)
        let gps_speed = true_speed + normal.sample(&mut rng) * cfg.sigma_gps_vel;
        let gps_beta = gps_speed / C;
        let measured_gamma_minus_1 = gps_beta.powi(2) / 2.0; // leading-order approx for small β

        // Uncertainty on γ−1 from speed uncertainty (propagated)
        // σ_{γ-1} = |∂(γ-1)/∂v| × σ_v ≈ (v/c²) × σ_v  (for small β)
        let sigma_gamma_minus_1 = (gps_speed / C.powi(2)) * cfg.sigma_gps_vel;

        // GPS timing: entry and exit timestamps
        let gps_entry = normal.sample(&mut rng) * cfg.sigma_gps_time;
        let gps_exit = true_transit + normal.sample(&mut rng) * cfg.sigma_gps_time;
        let gps_transit_time = gps_exit - gps_entry;
        let sigma_transit_time = (2.0_f64).sqrt() * cfg.sigma_gps_time;

        // Timing-based bound on |γ−1|:
        // If we tried to measure time dilation directly, the uncertainty in
        // transit time would limit our ability to detect the γ−1 effect.
        // The signal size is Δt × (γ−1).  To detect it, we need:
        //   Δt × |γ−1| > σ_Δt
        // → |γ−1| > σ_Δt / Δt
        // So a 1σ upper bound is:
        let bound_from_timing = sigma_transit_time / true_transit;

        trials.push(TrialResult {
            true_gamma_minus_1,
            measured_gamma_minus_1,
            sigma_gamma_minus_1,
            gps_transit_time,
            sigma_transit_time,
            bound_from_timing,
        });
    }

    // Compute ensemble statistics
    let mean_true: f64 = trials.iter().map(|t| t.true_gamma_minus_1).sum::<f64>() / cfg.n_trials as f64;
    let mean_measured: f64 = trials.iter().map(|t| t.measured_gamma_minus_1).sum::<f64>() / cfg.n_trials as f64;
    let mean_sigma: f64 = trials.iter().map(|t| t.sigma_gamma_minus_1).sum::<f64>() / cfg.n_trials as f64;
    let mean_bound_timing: f64 = trials.iter().map(|t| t.bound_from_timing).sum::<f64>() / cfg.n_trials as f64;

    // RMS of measured around true
    let rms_error: f64 = trials
        .iter()
        .map(|t| (t.measured_gamma_minus_1 - t.true_gamma_minus_1).powi(2))
        .sum::<f64>()
        / cfg.n_trials as f64;
    let rms_error = rms_error.sqrt();

    (trials, mean_bound_timing, rms_error)
}
